svg.title: xMind — one remote runtime, multiple independent views
svg.desc: Node A runs the native coding engine and workspace. Electron, browser, CLI and plugin viewers attach through an access gateway. WebRTC is a gateway and viewer transport with no dependency in the C++ agent core. Storage may be local or on xMind Server.
svg.text: xMind — execution stays on Node A; views can attach anywhere
Proposed boundary · UI and transport are independent of the agent / coding runtime
Independent viewers · nodes B, C, D and others
Electron standalone IDE
Browser / web view
VS Code / editor plugin
Console CLI / other client
Access gateway / transport adapters · outside the core
Authentication · signaling · WebRTC data channels · HTTPS / WebSocket adapters · subscriptions and reconnect
Existing Electron/WebRTC infrastructure can be reused here; the agent core has no Electron or WebRTC dependency.
Typed commands and durable events, independent of the chosen transport
Node A · xMind Runtime · C++ + embedded xlang3
General agents / graphs · coding engine · model adapters · MCP / A2A
Workspace files · shell / PTY · Git · diagnostics · tools / approvals
Run ownership · typed session state · durable events · policy enforcement
Runtime does not depend on a view being open
Node B can disconnect; Node C can resume observing the same run by event cursor.
View access and control/approval access are separate permissions.
Selected state location
Local on Node A
xlang3 → local SQLite
Shared xMind Server
Authenticated state service API
Server xlang3 → server SQLite
Views consume authorized state through APIs.
WebRTC carries the interaction; it does not own execution or persistence
Common command/event schemas work across transports. Reconnect must not replay non-idempotent tools or restart the runtime.
